extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners preparing or reviewing PCT/international application abstracts
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting the abstract for a PCT/international patent application (and complying with 37 CFR 1.438 and PCT Rule 8), including content, form, length, figure accompaniment, and presentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of the disclosure (technical field, problem, solution, uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall consist of a summary of the disclosure as contained in the description, the claims, and any drawings; the summary shall indicate the technical field to which the invention pertains and shall be drafted in a way which allows the clear understanding of the technical problem, the gist of the solution of that problem through the invention, and the principal use or uses of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core content requirement under PCT Rule 8; emphasize what is new in the art, clearly state the technical problem, summarize how the invention solves it, and list principal uses so that a reader can understand whether to consult the full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of characteristic chemical formula (when applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, the chemical formula which, among all the formulae contained in the international application, best characterizes the invention should be included in the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the single chemical formula that best characterizes the invention when chemical formulas are part of the disclosure (PCT Rule 8(a)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and word limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall be as concise as the disclosure permits (preferably 50 to 150 words if it is in English or when translated into English). National practice also provides a maximum of 150 words for the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the PCT preferred range of 50–150 words; avoid expanding beyond 150 words as publication problems may result. As a rule of thumb, the abstract (plus one drawing if included) should fit on an A4 sheet of typewritten matter, 1.5 spaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content: no claims of merit or speculative applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall not contain statements on the alleged merits or value of the claimed invention or on its speculative application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include promotional language, statements of superiority, speculation about future uses, or other assertions of value. Also avoid superfluous language and legal phraseology (see related entry). Prohibited items defined in PCT Rule 9 must not appear in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid certain wording and legal phraseology
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be primarily related to what is new in the art. Phrases should not be used which are implicit (for instance, 'the invention relates to...'), and statements on the alleged merits or value of the invention are not allowed. Avoid legal phraseology such as 'said' and 'means.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep language neutral, factual, and focused on technical content rather than legal or promotional expressions. Remove unnecessary boilerplate and journalistic or marketing-style phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference signs for technical features illustrated in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each main technical feature mentioned in the abstract and illustrated by a drawing in the international application shall be followed by a reference sign, placed between parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring to elements that appear in drawings, include the corresponding reference numerals in parentheses immediately after the feature name to aid clarity in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures accompanying the abstract (selection rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant fails to indicate a figure or if the International Searching Authority (ISA) finds that different figure(s) better characterize the invention, the ISA shall indicate which figure(s) should accompany the abstract when published. If the ISA finds none of the figures useful for the abstract, the abstract shall be published without any figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may suggest figure(s) under PCT Rule 3.3(a)(iii); the ISA can select alternative figures that better characterize the invention. If the ISA establishes the abstract, the applicant may propose modifications or comment until one month from the date of mailing of the international search report (PCT Rule 38.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Function as an efficient scanning/search tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall be so drafted that it can efficiently serve as a scanning tool for purposes of searching in the particular art, especially by assisting the scientist, engineer or researcher in formulating an opinion on whether there is a need for consulting the international application itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the abstract to enable quick assessment by a technical reader; include the minimal set of technical features and terms necessary for retrieval and evaluation in prior-art searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical placement and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract of the international application as filed must begin on a new sheet following the claims (Administrative Instructions Section 207). Other physical requirements must correspond to those for the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the abstract starts on a separate sheet placed after the claims; follow the same paper/formatted requirements as the description. Keep volume limited (see word/size guidance) so it fits publication formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative consequences for missing or non-compliant abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of an abstract upon filing of an international application will not affect the granting of a filing date. However, failure to furnish an abstract within one month from the date of the notification by the Receiving Office will result in the international application being declared withdrawn. The receiving Office or the ISA may invite the applicant to furnish or correct the abstract; the ISA may establish an abstract if applicant fails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invited to supply or correct the abstract, comply within the time limit; if the ISA establishes the abstract, applicants have a limited opportunity (e.g., one month from mailing of the international search report) to comment or propose modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary checklist (A–F) of required/expected items
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferably 50–150 words. Should contain: (A) Indication of field of invention. (B) Clear indication of the technical problem. (C) Summary of invention’s solution of the problem. (D) Principal use or uses of the invention. (E) Reference numbers of the main technical features placed between parentheses. (F) Where applicable, chemical formula which best characterizes the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this compact checklist as a drafting template to ensure the abstract contains all expected elements; cross-check against PCT Rule 8 and the MPEP guidance when preparing the abstract.
